# E02 T1 implementation report

This report describes the branch after the build review fix round and the production composition, merged with main
at 2db850d. The hub gates of docs/build/E02/T1.gates pass on that merge (table below). The E02 suite has 141 hub
and eval tests plus the 25 Vitest and 7 Playwright tests of the crew app, with no skips, xfails, deselections or
silenced checks. Branch coverage of E02 domain and application code is 95.43 percent. The whole hub suite ran 2011 tests: 2010
passed and one E17 timing test failed once under load (gate 7 below).

E02 is built and composed into the served hub. Sign-in, sessions, roster, credentials, adapter tokens, the attempt
limits, consent grants with their time fences, the record authorization binding, the owner and operator consoles and
the crew app session lock are complete. `app/privacy.py` registers E02's security and an adapter for each consumer
port (catchup, help, kit map, ground link, measurement, plans, roles, teach, events, records, config) under the
consumer's own port class, so production no longer runs on `DenySecurity` and `ClosedSessions`. Everything is tested
against real SQLite, real Argon2id, the real E01 `create_app` with its first start, and a real browser. The gaps
that remain belong to seams other epics own; each is filed in docs/requests/E02.md and fails closed today.

## Review fixes

Each finding of the build review has a regression test that fails on the code before the fix. They live in
hub/tests/privacy/test_review_fixes.py unless noted. Mutations of each fix were run by hand and every one was
killed by these tests; the only survivors were single halves of deliberate double guards (the high water term and
the high water check in `grants_now`, and the partition filter in SQL and in the domain), each killed when both
halves are removed.

1. Authorship granted permanent read access. The capture command now returns the record it accepted once, inside
   the command (app/assembly.py `_record_router`); `AuthoredRecords` and the author read-back rule are gone.
   A replay returns only the receipt, and only to its live author (`ReplayVisibility`).
   Tests: test_an_officer_capture_is_returned_once_and_never_read_again_without_consent,
   test_a_replayed_capture_reveals_only_its_receipt_and_only_to_its_live_author.
2. Console and owner authorization survived credential rotation. `verify_owner` returns an `OwnerProof` and
   `console_operator` an `OperatorProof`, each bound to the credential generation it verified; every mutation
   checks the generation again inside its own unit of work (`AccessGenerations`).
   Tests: test_an_operator_credential_rotated_during_its_proof_authorizes_no_console_command,
   test_an_owner_proof_dies_with_the_credential_it_verified.
3. Revocation did not fence an in flight read. `ConsentRecordAuthorization.require_read` decides again in a fresh
   snapshot after the read, with the session's liveness checked in that view (`SessionLiveness`). The test pauses a
   GET inside its snapshot and commits a revoke, and separately a credential change, before it continues.
   Tests: test_a_revocation_or_credential_change_committed_during_a_read_refuses_that_read,
   test_record_authorization_needs_the_session_live_in_the_deciding_view.
4. A read observed expiry could reverse. R-E02-21 as built: `grants_now` takes the clock admission (`TimeAdmission`)
   and refuses every finite grant while the clock is unknown or frozen, below tolerance regressions included, and
   measures time as the later of now and the durable high water, so an expiry once observed holds after a backward
   step even with zero snapshot writes and even when the regression fence failed to persist.
   Tests: test_a_read_observed_expiry_survives_a_backward_wall_step_with_zero_snapshot_writes,
   test_a_regression_below_the_tolerance_never_revives_an_expired_grant,
   test_a_regression_whose_fence_failed_to_persist_still_admits_no_finite_grant, and three domain tests in
   hub/tests/consent/test_grants_domain.py.
5. Grant mission and origin were ignored. A grant names its object partition, and a record grant releases an
   observation only when the stored observation's patient, mission and origin match (`ObservationPartitions`,
   filtered in SQL and again in the domain).
   Test: test_a_grant_must_name_its_object_partition_and_releases_only_inside_it.
6. Roster `from_day` and `until_day` were ignored. Membership is evaluated on the injected mission clock's day
   (`MissionDays`) for sign-in, authentication, consent and capture.
   Test: test_roster_days_bound_sign_in_sessions_consent_and_capture.
7. Nothing was composed in production, and catchup's scope was rejected. `app/station.py` `production` calls
   `privacy.compose`; `catchup/approved/1` is a valid consent object.
   Tests: test_catchups_exact_scope_is_a_valid_consent_object and hub/tests/privacy/test_composed.py.
8. Rate limit timing revealed principal existence. An unknown principal, a locked one and a wrong secret take the
   same path and the same verification cost from another client.
   Test: test_a_locked_principal_and_an_unknown_one_look_the_same_from_another_client.

Review gaps closed: replay is now proven through the HTTP command executor and the composed `ReplayVisibility`
(finding 1 tests), and event delivery after consent revocation is proven through the audience rule the delivery
consults per event, which admits a grantee while the grant is active and refuses after revocation
(test_consent_ports_follow_grants_and_events_stop_after_revocation_and_sign_out). Measurement events are person
scoped to the patient, so no grantee receives them over SSE today; the same test proves a stream ends at sign out.

## Production composition (app/privacy.py)

`compose` runs inside `production`'s `configure`, after module registration and before the fail closed stand-ins.
Each adapter is registered under the consumer's real port class, only when its dependencies are installed; a port
another composer already bound keeps its provider.

| Consumer port | E02 adapter |
|---|---|
| app `HttpSecurity`, `ConfigHttpMetadata` (replay visibility) | `IdentitySecurity`, `ReplayVisibility` |
| events `SessionAuthorizer` | `LiveSessions` |
| catchup `CatchupGate`, help `HelpGate`, groundlink `GroundLinkGate`, kitmap `KitmapRoles`, plans and roles authenticators | `SessionGate` (contract roles per operation) |
| teach `TeachAuthenticator`, measurement `MeasurementAuthenticator` | `HeaderGate`, `MeasurementGate` |
| help, roles and kitmap rosters, plans `PersonDirectory`, teach `RecordRouting` | roster adapters over `IdentityService` |
| catchup `CatchupConsent`, measurement `MeasurementConsent` | `ConsentAdapter` |
| consent `ObservationPartitions`, `TimeAdmission` | `ObservationsAdapter` (records store), `ClockAdmissionAdapter` |

hub/tests/privacy/test_composed.py proves each one over HTTP against the real app, allowed and denied:
test_production_registers_every_e02_adapter_under_its_consumers_port_class,
test_help_plans_roles_and_teach_admit_their_contract_roles_and_refuse_the_rest,
test_kitmap_groundlink_measurement_and_catchup_gates_are_e02s,
test_roster_people_and_routing_ports_answer_from_the_current_roster,
test_consent_ports_follow_grants_and_events_stop_after_revocation_and_sign_out,
test_each_consumer_gate_checks_the_contract_roles_itself_without_the_middleware. Kit map and ground link pass the
E02 gate and then answer their own SIM unavailability (no active environment, no ground link); catchup refuses every
session (R-E02-30).

## Built

Hub, identity (hub/src/crew_health/identity/)

- domain/session.py: principal kinds, roles from kind and officer rank only, session facts and liveness, lifetimes
  capped at `security.idle_lock_minutes` for people, oldest first replacement past `identity.sessions_per_principal`.
- domain/limits.py: principal, client and global attempt buckets with windowed debt, refund and reclaim, and one
  outcome for unknown and locked principals.
- domain/roster.py: whole document roster validation, member and principal ceilings, display names kept exactly,
  roster days.
- domain/routing.py: subject binding for manual capture (E02 3.4): self capture, or the acting medical officer
  entering for a named roster member; officer status grants no chart read.
- application/service.py: sign-in as a reservation unit of work, one bounded Argon2id verification outside the
  writer, then an issuance unit of work that rechecks principal, generation, verifier and the roster on the mission
  day; per request authentication; sign-out with the S5.8 ledger; restart and removal ending sessions; owner proofs;
  session liveness in a caller's view; the listCrew page.
- application/admin.py: roster bootstrap and change, credentials and adapter tokens, each command taking an
  `OperatorProof` checked again in its unit of work.
- application/settings.py, support.py, store.py, ports.py: settings, audit declarations, the store protocol and
  the ports other modules consume (`IdentityPorts` with `generations`, `SessionReader`, `SessionLiveness`,
  `AccessGenerations`, `HubProfile`).
- adapters/repository.py with migrations/0001_identity.sql, adapters/credentials.py (Argon2id at the design's fixed
  parameters, tokens stored only as digests), adapters/vault.py (`PrivateKeyVault` location, unavailable).
- api/router.py, cli.py, schemas/roster-bootstrap.schema.json, module.py (registration, audit policies, migration,
  startup sweep).

Hub, consent (hub/src/crew_health/consent/)

- domain/grants.py: owner only, prospective, exact grants over a named partition; `grants_now` denies any unknown or
  terminal fact, and a finite grant also needs an admitted clock, its issuing process epoch, an elapsed monotonic
  time below its span and the durable high water below its end.
- application/service.py: `allows` and `fields` with a `partition`, grant and revoke in the caller's unit of work
  with reference only audit, absolute expiry through S5.10, fences on correction, regression and restart, the owner
  listing; `RECORD_PURPOSE` lives here and records re-exports it.
- application/records.py: `ConsentRecordAuthorization(consent, capture, sessions, snapshots, bound)`: owner or
  explicit grant inside the observation's partition, officer capture for a current member, and the fresh snapshot
  re-decision with a live session.
- adapters/repository.py with migrations/0001_consent.sql, cli.py (owner console), module.py.

Hub, composition: app/privacy.py (new); app/assembly.py (`RegisteredSecurity`, the capture result returned once);
app/station.py (`production` calls `compose`).

Crew app (ui/crew/), unchanged in this round: src/features/identity/sessionLock.ts and the minimal E03 shell listed
under E03 owned files created.

Shared files changed: hub/pyproject.toml, hub/uv.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml (ui/crew importer), the generated manifests
(D26) and installed_modules.py regenerated from main's versions, hub/tests/app/test_installed_wheel.py and
test_serve.py (every packaged schema, and setting units E02 declares).

The fix round was committed, then origin/main at 2db850d (E17, model runtime) was merged. It touched no E02 file.
The only conflict was the generated installed_modules.py; the three generated files were taken from main and
regenerated (contracts build, TypeScript manifest, import contracts, package hashes), and a second regeneration left
no diff.

## Real and faked

Real: SQLite through E01's `SQLiteDatabase`; Argon2id at 64 MiB, 3 iterations, parallelism 4; E01's `create_app`
with `BuildCatalog.installed`, its real first start (migrations, the bootstrap release through the loader's checks,
clock wiring and sweep) and the operator's hub time confirmation; middleware, generated models, event delivery and
records. Real in Playwright: the hub over uvicorn, Vite and Chromium.

Faked or substituted:

- Time is `MemoryClock` (SIM clock at 2026-11-14T08:00Z) under PersistentClocks; the station appends the first
  mission clock version (R-E02-32).
- Resources are E01's `copy_station_resources` (tests/app/conftest.py): the repository's own first start release
  fails validation on main, which is not E02's to fix.
- The SIM roster comes from the package examples, loaded only by the test station.
- `RecordHttpServices` (observation policies, unit converter) is supplied by the station, over the real consent
  record authorization: production registers none (R-E02-31).
- The private vault is `UnavailableVault` (R-E02-20).
- Playwright signs in through the real `createSession` inside the page, because the sign-in words do not exist
  (X-E03-1).

## Changed exported names

For consumers, E04 (#39) included:

- `IdentityService.verify_owner` returns `OwnerProof`; `console_operator` returns `OperatorProof`; every admin
  command takes an `OperatorProof`.
- `ConsentService.grant`, `revoke` and `own_grants` accept `OwnerProof | SessionContext`.
- `ConsentQueries.allows` and `fields` take a `partition` keyword.
- `AuthoredRecords` is replaced by `ObservationPartitions` (with `ObservationFacts`).
- `ConsentRecordAuthorization` is constructed as `(consent, capture, sessions, snapshots, bound)`.
- `RosterEntry` gains `on_roster_until_day`; `RosterPort` gains `partition`.
- `IdentityPorts` gains `generations`.
- New: `SessionLiveness`, `AccessGenerations`, `OwnerProof`, `OperatorProof`, `TimeAdmission`, `ClockAdmission`.
- `RECORD_PURPOSE` moved to consent.application.service and is re-exported from records.

## Design corrections

1. Author read-back is replaced by the capture result returned once (finding 1). The design's read-back rule
   granted every later read; a command's own response is not a read grant.
2. Console and owner proofs are bound to credential generations and checked again in the mutation (finding 2).
3. A record read is decided twice, in the read's snapshot and in a fresh one with a live session (finding 3).
4. Finite grants follow R-E02-21 with the clock admission and the durable high water (finding 4).
5. Grants are scoped to an object partition with mission and origin (finding 5).
6. Roster days bound access on the mission clock (finding 6).
7. Console bootstrap trust: the physical console is trusted for the first roster document only.
8. Console commands are guarded by expected revisions and credential generations, not S5.8 command identity.
9. Adapter tokens are `identity_session` rows of kind adapter.
10. Roster removal is final.
11. Ground sign-in exists only when the composer provides `HubProfile` for a ground or demo hub.
12. A `deleteCurrentSession` retried with an ended token answers 401.
13. `SessionReader.alive` lets event delivery revalidate an open stream at each heartbeat.
14. The crew app checks its deadline on the monotonic and the wall clock, the earlier wins.
15. The owner listing returns every active grant and one page of the newest ended ones with an `older` flag.
16. Identity and consent refuse to start when `storage.max_rows` is 256 or less.
17. A roster change reads every current member and checks re-adds by exact person IDs.

## Limitations

- Catchup refuses every session until a ground recipient exists (R-E02-30); crew sign-in on a served hub fails
  closed until the first mission clock version exists (R-E02-32); a served hub has no observation routes
  (R-E02-31).
- The fresh snapshot read fence covers records only; other consumers decide in their own snapshot (R-E02-34).
- T-E02-002, 005, 017 and the configuration clauses of 021 wait on E26, E21, E09, E16, E29 and E20, as before.
- T-E02-006 and T-E02-014 are partial (no journal canary, no vault backend); T-E02-011 does not cover E03's offline
  queue; T-E02-016 covers a saturated verifier, not the emergency cache.
- The mutation checks were run by hand on the fixes; the repository has no mutation tool yet (R-E02-22).
